sentence: She _______ to work every day.
explanations: 'Walk' is the base form - needs third-person 's' with 'she'.
Correct! 'Walks' is the third-person singular present simple form.
'Walking' is the gerund/continuous form, not present simple.
'Walked' is past tense, but we need present for a daily habit.

sentence: They _______ coffee in the morning.
explanations: 'Drinks' needs a singular subject (he/she/it), but 'they' is plural.
'Drinking' is the gerund/continuous form, not present simple.
Correct! 'Drink' is the present simple form for plural subjects.
'Drank' is past tense, but we need present for a regular habit.

sentence: My brother _______ video games on weekends.
explanations: 'Play' is the base form - needs third-person 's' with 'brother'.
'Playing' is the gerund/continuous form, not present simple.
Correct! 'Plays' is third-person singular present simple.
'Played' is past tense, but we're talking about a regular activity.

sentence: I _______ for my keys right now.
explanations: 'Look' is present simple, but 'right now' indicates ongoing action.
'Looking' needs a helping verb (am/is/are) to form continuous tense.
Correct! 'Am looking' shows an action happening at this moment.
'Looked' is past tense, but the action is happening now.

sentence: The children _______ in the garden at the moment.
explanations: 'Play' is present simple, but we need continuous for 'at the moment'.
'Plays' is wrong - both tense and subject-verb agreement are off.
Correct! 'Are playing' describes an action in progress right now.
'Played' is past tense, but the action is currently happening.

sentence: She _______ a book this week.
explanations: 'Reads' is present simple for habits, not temporary activities.
Correct! 'Is reading' shows a temporary activity in progress.
'Read' (present) is simple tense, not continuous for 'this week'.
'Reading' needs 'is' to complete the present continuous structure.

sentence: We _______ to Paris last summer.
explanations: 'Go' is present tense, but 'last summer' requires past.
'Goes' is present tense third-person, wrong on both counts here.
Correct! 'Went' is the irregular past form of 'go'.
'Going' is the gerund/continuous form, needs helping verb.

sentence: She _______ her homework yesterday.
explanations: 'Finish' is present tense, but 'yesterday' requires past.
Correct! 'Finished' is the past simple form for completed actions.
'Finishes' is present tense, wrong for a past time marker.
'Finishing' is gerund/continuous, doesn't fit this context.

sentence: They _______ the movie last night.
explanations: 'Watch' is present tense, but 'last night' requires past.
'Watches' is present third-person singular, doubly wrong here.
Correct! 'Watched' is past simple for a completed past action.
'Watching' needs a helping verb and doesn't fit simple past.

sentence: I _______ never _______ sushi before.
explanations: 'Did eat' is past simple, but 'never...before' suggests present perfect.
Correct! 'Have eaten' connects past experience to the present.
'Am eating' is present continuous, wrong for life experience.
'Was eating' is past continuous, doesn't fit this context.

sentence: She _______ in London for five years.
explanations: 'Lives' is present simple, doesn't show the duration from past to now.
'Lived' is past simple, suggests she no longer lives there.
Correct! 'Has lived' shows an action that started in past, continues now.
'Is living' is present continuous, doesn't emphasize the five-year period.

sentence: They _______ their work yet.
explanations: 'Didn't finish' is past simple, but 'yet' typically pairs with present perfect.
'Don't finish' is present simple, doesn't work with 'yet' in this context.
Correct! 'Haven't finished' is present perfect, perfect with 'yet'.
'Aren't finishing' is present continuous, doesn't fit with 'yet' here.

sentence: I think it _______ rain tomorrow.
explanations: Correct! 'Will' is used for predictions and spontaneous decisions.
'Is going to' works for predictions, but 'will' is more natural with 'think'.
'Rains' is present simple, wrong for future prediction.
'Rained' is past tense, completely wrong context.

sentence: Don't worry, I _______ help you with that.
explanations: 'Am going to' suggests planning, but this is a spontaneous offer.
Correct! 'Will' is perfect for promises and instant decisions.
'Help' is present simple, doesn't express future intention.
'Helped' is past tense, makes no sense here.

sentence: Look at those clouds! It _______ rain soon.
explanations: 'Will' works for predictions, but 'going to' is better with visible evidence.
Correct! 'Is going to' is used for predictions based on present evidence.
'Rains' is present simple, doesn't indicate future.
'Rained' is past tense, wrong time frame.

sentence: We _______ visit our grandparents this weekend.
explanations: 'Will' can work, but 'going to' better shows prior planning.
Correct! 'Are going to' indicates a planned future action.
'Visit' is present simple, doesn't express future plan.
'Visited' is past tense, wrong time reference.

sentence: If it _______ tomorrow, we will stay home.
explanations: Correct! First conditional uses present simple in the 'if' clause.
'Will rain' is wrong - we don't use 'will' in the 'if' clause.
'Rained' is past tense, first conditional needs present.
'Raining' needs a helping verb and doesn't fit the structure.

sentence: If you study hard, you _______ the exam.
explanations: 'Pass' is present simple, but main clause needs 'will' for future result.
Correct! First conditional uses 'will' + base verb in the main clause.
'Passed' is past tense, doesn't fit conditional structure.
'Passing' is gerund form, doesn't complete the conditional.

sentence: If I _______ a million dollars, I would travel the world.
explanations: 'Have' is present tense, second conditional needs past simple.
'Has' is present third-person, wrong tense for this conditional.
Correct! Second conditional uses past simple in the 'if' clause.
'Having' is gerund form, doesn't fit conditional structure.

sentence: If she _______ harder, she would get better grades.
explanations: 'Study' is base form, second conditional needs past simple.
'Studies' is present tense, wrong for hypothetical situation.
Correct! Second conditional uses past simple to show it's hypothetical.
'Studying' is gerund, doesn't complete the conditional structure.
